derivations.claim: For an integer $r$ with $0<|r|<2\ell$, put $C_r=\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}\cos(rm\pi/\ell)$. If $r$ is odd, the geometric sum of $e^{i\pi rm/\ell}$ for $0\le m<2\ell$ is zero. Pairing terms at $m$ and $2\ell-m$ for $1\le m\le\ell-1$ leaves twice $C_r$; the two unpaired real terms are $1+\cos(r\pi)=0$, so $C_r=0$. Also $C_0=\ell-1$.

The product-to-sum identity gives the left side as $\tfrac12(C_{a-b}-C_{a+b})$, with $C_0$ used when $a=b$. If $a=b$, then $a+b$ is nonzero even and less than $2\ell$, so the value is $\tfrac12((\ell-1)-(-1))=\ell/2$. If $a\ne b$ and $a,b$ have the same parity, both nonzero indices $a-b$ and $a+b$ are even and their $C$ values are $-1$; if they have opposite parity, both indices are odd and their values are $0$. $\bigl(L_2\cap(L_3+L_1)\bigr)^\perp =L_2+(L_3+L_1)^\perp=L_2+(L_1\cap L_3).$

$a\in L_2+(L_1\cap L_3).$
